description: Separate strengths and weaknesses from external opportunities and threats.
accomplishes: Separate strengths and weaknesses from external opportunities and threats. Attach evidence or an explicit assumption label to each item. Prioritise decisions and validation needs rather than filling four boxes with unsupported statements.
prompt:
Act as a business strategy adviser.

Task: Create an evidence-based SWOT.

Input context:
- BUSINESS: [BUSINESS]
- INTERNAL DATA: [INTERNAL DATA]
- EXTERNAL SOURCES: [EXTERNAL SOURCES]

Separate strengths and weaknesses from external opportunities and threats. Attach evidence or an explicit assumption label to each item. Prioritise decisions and validation needs rather than filling four boxes with unsupported statements.

Distinguish verified facts, assumptions and scenarios. Example values are not verified market data.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Fictional workshop SWOT
| Quadrant | Item | Status |
| Strength | Documented registration process | Needs source check |
| Weakness | Scattered manual follow-up | Supplied description |
| Opportunity | Possible demand for short classes | Hypothesis |
| Threat | Dependence on one channel | Risk to measure |
Check channel concentration before recommending diversification; no market study is claimed.
